one_liner: Computer-vision library whose cv::resize upscaling and cv::GaussianBlur ran 3-17x faster than ImageMagick 6.9, single-threaded.
what_it_does: OpenCV is a general computer-vision library; for this category the relevant pieces are imgproc's cv::resize (nearest, bilinear, bicubic, area, Lanczos4) and cv::GaussianBlur on in-memory cv::Mat images, plus imgcodecs for load and save. It is not a drop-in for ImageMagick: you call C++ (or Python cv2) functions on BGR-ordered Mats with explicit interpolation flags, kernel size and sigma, instead of running a convert/magick command line or a Wand/MagickWand object. Colour management, format breadth and most ImageMagick operators have no direct equivalent.
how_it_is_fast: 8-bit INTER_LINEAR resize is a separable two-pass filter with precomputed integer coefficient tables (INTER_RESIZE_COEF_BITS = 11), a horizontal pass into an int row buffer and a SIMD vertical pass (VResizeLinearVec_32s8u), and it always reads only 2x2 source pixels, which is also why it does not antialias on shrinking. INTER_AREA has a SIMD box-average fast path for integer factors (ResizeAreaFastVec_SIMD_8u) and precomputed overlap weights otherwise. 8-bit GaussianBlur runs a bit-exact separable fixed-point filter (ufixedpoint16, 8 fractional bits) with symmetric-kernel folding and special 3- and 5-tap kernels, split over rows with parallel_for_ and compiled for several ISAs with runtime CPU dispatch (CV_CPU_DISPATCH). In the measured 4.1.2 build, cv::resize first tried Intel IPP's iwiResize when OpenCV was built with IPP (WITH_IPP defaults to ON on x86), which IPP accepts for 8-bit INTER_CUBIC and INTER_LANCZOS4 but not for 8-bit bilinear, area or nearest, so the bicubic and Lanczos rows may be IPP code rather than OpenCV's own kernels. Current 4.x routes this through hal/ipp (ipp_hal_resize).
when_to_use: Upscaling 8-bit RGB images in-process where bilinear or bicubic quality is enough: pillow-perf measured 57.7 ms (bilinear) and 115.3 ms (bicubic) for 2560x1600 to 5478x3424 on one Haswell core, versus 1007.6 and 1256.1 ms for ImageMagick 6.9.
Small-sigma Gaussian blur on 8-bit images (sigma about 1, 7-tap window): 69 ms vs 675 ms for ImageMagick on a 4 MP frame, single-threaded.
Integer-factor downscales with INTER_AREA (box averaging), e.g. 2560x1600 to 320x200 in 5.4 ms, when a box filter is an acceptable shrink filter.
Pipelines that already link OpenCV for vision work, where adding ImageMagick only for resize or blur would add a second heavy dependency.

Multi-core servers: resize and GaussianBlur split rows across threads with parallel_for_ (pthreads by default); the catalogued numbers were taken with cv2.setNumThreads(1), so default runs can be faster.
when_not_to_use: Quality downscaling with bilinear or bicubic: cv::resize does no antialiasing, and the OpenCV docs advise INTER_AREA for shrinking; an antialiased resize is still an open feature request (#25620). Convolution resamplers such as Pillow-SIMD, libvips or fast_image_resize are the like-for-like choice.

Large-sigma Gaussian blur: the separable filter costs O(window) per pixel, so sigma 30 (151 taps) took 1.40 s, while Pillow 7.0.0 in the same pillow-perf file stays at about 0.19 s at every radius and Pillow-SIMD AVX2 bicubic upscale (76.6 ms) also beats OpenCV's 115.3 ms.

OpenCV builds older than 4.2.0 for 8-bit GaussianBlur with large windows: the fixed-point kernel was rounded tap by tap without renormalising, so output came out darker (issue #9863: ksize 151, sigma 30, about 10 percent darker).
JPEG-heavy pipelines judged on codec speed: pillow-perf shows OpenCV slower than ImageMagick at JPEG load (47.9 vs 27.4 ms) and save (56.7 vs 48.0 ms).
Projects that need a small dependency, colour management, or the format breadth of ImageMagick.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (CMake build of opencv_core + opencv_imgproc; prebuilt opencv-python wheels and distro packages)
integration.dependencies: imgproc needs only opencv_core; optional Intel IPP ICV on x86 (WITH_IPP on by default except MinGW), TBB or OpenMP (off by default; pthreads parallel_for is on), Carotene and KleidiCV HALs on ARM, image codec libraries for imgcodecs
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 for the 4.x line, C++17 for the 5.x line (default branch); CMake 3.7+ for 4.x
integration.platforms: x86-64 with runtime dispatch up to AVX2/AVX-512, AArch64 (NEON, Carotene, KleidiCV), RISC-V and others
integration.thread_safety: Not documented in the files read. Functions work on caller-owned Mats; the internal parallel_for_ pool is a process-wide setting changed with cv::setNumThreads.

gotchas: Different filters under the same names: OpenCV INTER_CUBIC uses a = -0.75 (and the 4.1.2 IPP path is configured to match), while ImageMagick's catrom is a = -0.5; INTER_LANCZOS4 is an 8x8 Lanczos-4 kernel, not ImageMagick's Lanczos-3; INTER_AREA acts like nearest neighbour when enlarging.

8-bit results come from fixed-point arithmetic (11-bit resize coefficients, 8-bit-fraction Gaussian taps): at large sigma each Gaussian tap is only a few 1/256 steps, and plain INTER_LINEAR is not the bit-exact mode (INTER_LINEAR_EXACT is).
When ksize is 0, GaussianBlur derives it from sigma with 3 sigma per side for 8-bit images but 4 sigma for float images, so 8-bit and float blurs of the same sigma use different windows.

imread returns BGR channel order, and resize with interpolation code 0 is nearest neighbour; third-party benchmarks that pass 0 (as the speedtest-resize go-opencv row does) are not measuring bilinear.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick OpenCV over Pillow-SIMD, libvips or fast_image_resize when you already depend on it or need fast bilinear upscaling and small-kernel blurs inside a vision pipeline; pick those convolution resamplers when downscale quality matters, and pick a box-blur approximation (FastBoxBlur, LibGaussianBlur, Pillow) for large-radius blurs. For a whole load-resize-save pipeline, libvips (0.57 s) is far ahead of OpenCV (3.15 s) in the same libvips wiki table.
verified_claims_summary: pillow-perf (run by the Pillow-SIMD authors) timed the opencv-python 4.1 binary wheel against ImageMagick 6.9 through Wand on one Core i5-4430 core (Ubuntu 18.04.3, both libraries forced single-threaded, compiler and flags not stated) on a 2560x1600 RGB image: like-for-like upscale to 5478x3424 is 17.5x faster bilinear and 10.9x faster bicubic, and Gaussian blur is 9.7x, 4.0x and 2.9x faster at sigma 1, 10 and 30. Reading the 4.1.2 source shows the sigma 10 and 30 blur rows ran a kernel whose 8-bit fixed-point taps summed to 254/256 and 243/256 per pass (computed from getFixedpointGaussianKernel, matching issue #9863's 10 percent darkening at ksize 151, sigma 30), a bug fixed in 4.2.0 by error-diffusion quantisation; the fix changes coefficients, not the code path, so the timings are probably still representative, but the measured output was wrong. Separately, the libvips wiki pipeline (crop, 0.9x resize, sharpen, TIFF load and save on a 16-core Threadripper PRO 3955WX, Ubuntu 25.04 packages) has OpenCV 4.10 at 3.15 s against multi-threaded ImageMagick 7.1.1 at 4.41 s (1.4x).
status_note: Very active (last commit 2026-10-02 on 4.x, default branch 5.x, 91.1k stars) and Apache-2.0; usable directly from wheels or distro packages, but the catalogued pillow-perf numbers come from a 2019-2020 opencv-python 4.1 wheel.
